- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak by 2–5% relative to model output.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+3% from prior day), model often overshoots; cap forecast for next 3–5 days at 1–2% below peak.
- If sentiment is consistently negative or neutral (≤0.3), model underestimates; add 1–3% to forecast mean to compensate for downward bias.
- Model frequently overpredicts early in 30-day horizon; apply 1–3% downward adjustment to first 5–7 days of forecast.
- When sentiment history shows strong recent reversal (e.g., 0.00 → 1.00 → 0.00), model often fails to adjust; reduce forecast slope toward mean of last 5–7 days.
- If model forecast is >+5% above recent 18-day average, flag for correction — reduce by 1–3% unless sentiment supports continuation.
- Sentiment spikes (≥0.8) in last 3 days correlate with model overestimation; apply 1–2% downward correction to forecast peak.
- Model underestimates when sentiment is low but price is trending up — adjust forecast upward by 1–2% if sentiment is 0.2–0.4 and price is rising.
